message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average) |
| **Molar mass** | 1.008 g mol⁻¹ |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Valence electrons** | 1 |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (¹H, 0 n), Deuterium (²H, 1 n, stable), Tritium (³H, 2 n, β‑radioactive, t½ ≈ 12.32 y) |
| **Density (STP)** | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (−434.3 °F) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (–423.17 °F) |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **Ionization energy (1st)** | 13.598 eV |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV |
| **Covalent radius** | 31 pm |
| **Van der Waals radius** | 120 pm |
| **Atomic radius** | 53 pm |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas |
| **Color / Odor / Taste** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless |
| **Flammability** | Highly flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (2–9 % H₂ in air) |
| **Diffusivity** | Extremely high (fastest among gases) |
| **Reactivity** | Forms hydrides (e.g., LiH, CaH₂), acids (e.g., HCl, H₂SO₄), and many organohydrogen compounds |
| **Common compounds** | H₂O, NH₃, CH₄, H₂S, HF, H₂O₂, H₂CO₃, etc. |
| **Uses** | Fuel cells, rocket propellant, ammonia synthesis (Haber process), hydrogenation reactions, metallurgy, semiconductor processing, medical imaging (PET with ¹⁸F), etc. |
| **Abundance** | Most abundant element in the Universe (~75 % by mass), but only ~0.000055 % of Earth’s atmosphere |

---

### Quick Summary

- **Simplest element**: One proton, one electron; no neutrons in the most common isotope (protium).
- **Physical state**: Gas at standard conditions; extremely light (density < 0.1 g L⁻¹).
- **Chemical behavior**: Diatomic (H₂) under normal conditions; highly reactive, forming a wide range of compounds.
- **Isotopic significance**: Deuterium is used in nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and as a tracer; tritium is a radioactive isotope used in fusion research and radiolabeling.
- **Industrial importance**: Central to the Haber process, fuel cells, and many chemical syntheses.

These properties make hydrogen unique among elements, both as the simplest building block of matter and as a versatile component in modern technology and industry.
